title: Predicted higher harmonics reduce pooled GJ 674 error by 2.5 percent in five HARPS seasons
abstract: We test higher harmonics of an eccentric GJ 674 orbit against two circular signals at exact 2:1. Four seasons train an exact orbit; its harmonics at three or more times the orbital frequency predict the held season. In 224 HARPS-RVBank v02 exposures, pooled weighted squared error falls by 2.52 percent. Conditional null tests refit training orbits in 399 draws per error-block width. Upper-tail fractions are 0.005, 0.010 and 0.0075 for 1-, 10- and 30-day blocks. Six extraction and activity controls keep pooled gains of 1.43 to 2.47 percent. The 2006 gain is negative in every setting. This extends an earlier two-season test. It gives limited support under restricted models and unverified sign-error assumptions. No new planet or independent-instrument confirmation is established. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and a retrieval recipe are included; external data remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Higher-harmonic predictions reduce pooled squared error by 2.52 percent but fail in 2006. Right: conditional two-circular null scores with training-orbit refits. These tests assume independent sign-symmetric error blocks.

citations.reason: Extends the two-season higher-harmonic test to five held-season predictions and null pipeline refits.
Uses dense-season selection and fixed periods; tests higher harmonics rather than the second harmonic.
Reviews the null orbital H-alpha result as activity context.
